source_document.body:
Aerial view of the Cusi project area in Mexico. Credit: Silverco Mining.
By: Northern Miner Staff November 26, 2026
Silverco Mining (TSXV: SICO, US-OTC: SICOF) secured up to $15 million (C$21.3 million) in financing tied to concentrate sales from its newly restarted Cusi mine in Mexico, giving the company more room to fund the ramp-up of two underground operations through the first half of 2027. The stock rose.
The agreement, disclosed late Wednesday along with third-quarter results , follows Cusi’s first concentrate shipment on Nov. 16. Silverco aims to declare commercial production in the first half of next year at both Cusi in Chihuahua state and La Negra in Querétaro state, where a new underground fleet and tailings filtration plant are central to lifting mill throughput.
Shares of Silverco rose 6% to C$7.30 Thursday afternoon in Toronto, having earlier gained as much as 7.1%. That valued the company at about C$408 million ($287 million).
Silverco’s quarterly loss of 2¢ per share was narrower than the 8¢ average loss forecast by financial analysts, largely because costs came in below estimates.
“Our focus at La Negra remains on watching for unit costs to come down and grades to rise as productivity improvements are completed, translating into stronger margins, supplemented by the ramp-up at Cusi,” National Bank Capital Markets analyst Alex Terentiew wrote in a Thursday note. “Grade improvement remains central to our La Negra outlook.”
Nuevo deal
Higher throughput and recoveries at La Negra helped offset a silver grade of 49 grams per tonne, below Terentiew’s 55-gram forecast. Cash costs at the operation averaged about $54 per silver-equivalent oz., higher than a previous estimate of $50, the analyst said.
Silverco acquired La Negra in May through its all-share purchase of Nuevo Silver. In its first full quarter under Silverco, the mine processed 125,000 tonnes and produced 161,741 oz. of silver. Copper, lead and zinc brought total output to 348,578 silver-equivalent ounces. La Negra generated C$24.6 million in revenue and C$3.4 million in mine operating earnings. Silverco ended September with C$36.2 million in cash.
La Negra averaged about 1,360 tonnes per day over the quarter, just over half its 2,500-tonne design capacity.
The first unit of its new Epiroc fleet, an underground development drill, has arrived, and Silverco has awarded the civil works contract for the filtration plant. The company expects filtered tailings to ease the water-management constraint that limits mill throughput. It is targeting commissioning by the end of June.
Mine extension
Exploration could also extend the reach of the existing mine. On Tuesday, Silverco reported that a surface hole at Valenciana, about 650 metres northwest of La Negra’s mine infrastructure, cut 15.65 metres grading 322 grams silver per tonne from 224 metres depth. Underground drilling also extended mineralization down dip at the Valeria and Brecha deposits.
At Cusi, which had been on care and maintenance since September 2023, Silverco says the $19.2-million restart remains on budget. The company plans to hand over the refurbished Mal Paso mill to operations by the end of November and start extracting ore from its first stope at Promontorio late this quarter. Underground development continues at San Miguel as Silverco works toward the mill’s design rate of 1,200 tonnes per day.
Silverco can draw on the Cusi prepayment facility at its discretion, with each draw repayable over 24 months. The company says the two mines could deliver more than 4 million silver-equivalent oz. in 2027, based on their preliminary economic assessments.
